header.name: The Business of Artificial Intelligence
header.description:
Artificial Intelligence is clearly creating waves as firms, big and small, rush to launch new products, solutions, and companies. However, the question remains as to how to create a sustainable business from AI? Converting technology into a tangible, viable business proposition requires an extensive understanding of customer behaviour, competitive landscape, business models and ability to execute towards a tangible product market fit. The evolution of human-machine interactions from a context where the human adapts to the machine and the machine does not (i.e., traditional human-machine interaction), to a context where the human and the machine learn from and adapt to each other requires conceptualization about the nature of relationships consumers have with AI-driven products. The course focuses on evolving human - machine interactions, its implications on design, product development, and ability to create and grow a viable business.

This course is NOT restricted to those who want to become an entrepreneur (though they are welcome to join). Developing new businesses out of emerging technologies is a problem not unique to startups, but also faced by established firms. Otherwise, every innovation from giants like Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Apple, Meta, IBM and others would have been successful. The course is meant for those who may like to explore the combination of technology and business knowledge sometime in their career.

It is becoming increasingly clear that the business leader of tomorrow (& today) needs to have both technical and business acumen. At the time business schools are nudging students to be more technology proficient, it is important for graduates from technology universities to be exposed to business skills.

The course leverages and builds upon the core thinking behind some of the courses from Stanford School of Engineering - Building an AI-Enabled Organization, Business Model Innovation, Management Science and Ethics of Artificial Intelligence. Using a combination of management principles, case studies, real life use cases and instructor’s own 28 years global experiences as a tech corporate leader, entrepreneur and investor, the course focuses on the nuances of making a AI technology business successful.
